title: Literal common-stage internal Hom objects and normalized comparisons
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and any scheme $W$. Use the rational constructible stages of [def-sf-finite-rational-derived-operations] and the common-stage category of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. For a pair $P=((E,K)^{\mathrm{op}},(F,N))$, put $J=EF$, the finite compositum of [def-weil-finite-subextension-directed-set]. A pair is permitted when its two extensions to $J$ satisfy the integral-Hom constructibility predicate. Its Hom object is the literal pair $(J,R\mathcal Hom_J(K_J,N_J))$. This pair remains permitted after extension to every finite $L\supseteq J$. Identify the scalar extension of its output with $R\mathcal Hom_L(K_L,N_L)$ by the specified rational Hom scalar comparison, with the inverse first-input and forward second-input associators. The recorded transition identification is the equality from the stage-system specification. These are the already existing definitions, moved without changing their expressions.

proof.text: Retain the literal stage-system transition identification and the compositum Hom-pair, output and comparison definitions. They are the existing expressions, with no new choice or coefficient hypothesis.

Scalar extension preserves permitted integral Hom pairs. The two integral scalar associators identify their extended inputs with the inputs extended directly from their initial stages. Apply the integral internal-Hom functor to the inverse first associator and the forward second one. Constructibility is invariant under this isomorphism, so the direct pair at every larger stage is permitted.

theorem commonStageHomPairAtStage_permitted (W : Scheme.{u})
    (P : (commonStageHomPairs l Ω W).FullSubcategory)
    (L : Index l Ω) (h : (commonStageHomObject l Ω W P).stage ≤ L) :
    constructibleRationalHomPairs l (Coefficient.{u} l Ω L) W
      (op (P.obj.1.unop.toStage
        (((Padic.finiteCoefficientFields_properties l Ω).1
          P.obj.1.unop.stage P.obj.2.stage).1.trans h)),
        P.obj.2.toStage (((Padic.finiteCoefficientFields_properties l Ω).1
          P.obj.1.unop.stage P.obj.2.stage).2.trans h))
